questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised type of software maintenance?
questions.e: Corrective fixes faults, adaptive adjusts to a new environment and perfective improves features or performance. Regressive is not a standard category of maintenance.

questions.q: What is the full form of RAD in software engineering?
questions.e: RAD is Rapid Application Development, a high-speed adaptation of the waterfall model using component-based construction.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. Verification checks that the product meets the customer's actual needs.
II. Verification checks that the product conforms to its specification.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Verification asks 'Are we building the product right?', which means checking conformance to the specification. Checking against the customer's actual needs is validation, so I is false.

questions.q: Black box testing is also known as
questions.e: Black box testing checks behaviour against the specification without looking at the code. Structural, glass box and path testing are white box terms.

questions.q: In software configuration management, a baseline is
o: a formally reviewed work product that can be changed only through formal change control
the first draft of the SRS
the cost estimate of the project
questions.e: A baseline is an approved configuration item that acts as the basis for further development. After that, changes need formal change control.

questions.q: In software reliability measurement, POFOD stands for
questions.e: POFOD is the probability that the system fails when a service request is made. It suits systems such as protection systems.

questions.q: Estimating by lines of code, the optimistic, most likely and pessimistic sizes are 20, 30 and 70 KLOC. Expected size is (opt + 4 × likely + pess) / 6. If the productivity is 500 LOC per person-month and the labour cost is ₹40,000 per person-month, the estimated cost is
questions.e: Expected size = (20 + 120 + 70) / 6 = 35 KLOC. Effort = 35000 / 500 = 70 person-months. Cost = 70 × 40,000 = ₹28,00,000.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an element of a data flow diagram?
questions.e: A DFD has processes, data stores, data flows and external entities. Inheritance belongs to object-oriented class models.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of feasibility study?
questions.e: Feasibility is judged as technical, economic, operational (and schedule or legal). Syntactic feasibility is not a standard type.

questions.q: The V-model of software development is an extension of the
questions.e: The V-model bends the waterfall model upward after coding to show that each testing phase corresponds to a development phase.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. Top-down integration testing uses stubs to replace lower-level modules.
II. Bottom-up integration testing uses drivers to call the modules under test.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Top-down integration begins with the main module, so missing subordinates are replaced by stubs. Bottom-up begins with low-level modules, so drivers are needed to call them. Both are correct.

questions.q: Which type of coupling is the loosest and most desirable between modules?
questions.e: Data coupling, where modules communicate only by passing simple data parameters, is the weakest coupling.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of cohesion?
questions.e: Stamp is a type of coupling, where modules share a composite data structure. Coincidental, logical and temporal are all types of cohesion.

questions.q: Upper CASE tools mainly support
questions.e: Upper CASE (front-end) tools support requirements, analysis and design. Lower CASE tools support coding, testing and maintenance.

questions.q: A system has an MTBF of 200 hours and an MTTR of 10 hours. Taking MTBF = MTTF + MTTR and availability = MTTF / (MTTF + MTTR), its availability is
questions.e: MTTF = MTBF − MTTR = 190 hours. Availability = 190 / (190 + 10) = 190 / 200 = 95%. The 95.2% figure wrongly takes 200 as the MTTF.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a UML diagram?
questions.e: The entity–relationship diagram belongs to database design and is not part of UML. Use case, class and sequence diagrams are standard UML diagrams.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a practice of Extreme Programming (XP)?
o: Detailed upfront design of the whole system
questions.e: XP favours small releases and a design that evolves through refactoring, not a detailed design of the whole system before coding. Pair programming, refactoring and continuous integration are core XP practices.

questions.q: A project has 10 external inputs (weight 4), 5 external outputs (weight 5), 4 external inquiries (weight 4), 3 internal logical files (weight 10) and 2 external interface files (weight 7). The sum of the 14 complexity ratings ΣFi is 30. Using FP = UFP × (0.65 + 0.01 × ΣFi), the function points are
In Basic COCOMO, the effort equation is E = a(KLOC)^b person-months. For an embedded project (a = 3.6, b = 1.20) of exactly 1 KLOC, the effort is
questions.e: With KLOC = 1, 1 raised to any power is 1, so E = a = 3.6 person-months.

questions.q: Which process model is most suitable when the customer cannot clearly state the requirements at the start?
questions.e: A prototype is shown to the user to elicit and refine unclear requirements. The waterfall and V-models assume stable requirements.

questions.q: In a structure chart, the number of modules that directly call a given module is called its
questions.e: Fan-in is the number of immediate superordinate modules that call a module, while fan-out is the number of modules it calls.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. White box testing requires knowledge of the internal code structure.
II. Equivalence partitioning is a white box testing technique.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: White box testing designs tests from the internal logic, so I is true. Equivalence partitioning derives tests from input classes of the specification, so it is black box and II is false.

questions.q: Another name for the waterfall model is the
questions.e: The waterfall model is also called the classical life cycle or linear sequential model. Iterative enhancement is the incremental approach.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a mode of the Basic COCOMO model?
questions.e: Basic COCOMO classifies projects as organic, semi-detached or embedded.

questions.q: A field accepts ages from 18 to 60 inclusive. Which set of test values corresponds to boundary value analysis, including values just outside the range?
questions.e: BVA tests on and next to each boundary: 17, 18, 19 at the lower end and 59, 60, 61 at the upper end.
